Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 30, verse 9–11:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have they not travelled in the land?﴾ That is: have they not journeyed and looked upon the places where the earlier nations met their end, how they were destroyed because of their denial, so that they might take heed?

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and they tilled the land﴾ That is: they turned it over for cultivation, and from this the cow is called "muthirah" (one that stirs up the soil). Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Mu'adh al-Qari', and Abu Haywah read: "wa-atharū al-arḍa" with a long alif after the hamza and a fatha on the thaʼ, with the rā' in the nominative (raf'), ﴿and they cultivated it more than they cultivated it﴾ That is: more than the people of Makkah cultivate it, owing to the long lifespans of those people and the strength of their power. ﴿And their messengers came to them with the clear proofs﴾ That is: with the evidences. ﴿So Allah would not have wronged them﴾ by punishing them without fault. (p-291) ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾ by disbelief and denial. This indicates that they did not believe and so were destroyed.

Then He informed about their end, saying: ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was the worst﴾ meaning the evil outcome, and there are two views concerning it. One: that it is the punishment, related by al-Hasan. The second: that it is Hell, related by al-Suddi.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿that they denied﴾ Al-Farra' said: its meaning is "because they denied," and when the lam was dropped it became in the accusative. Al-Zajjaj said: because of their denial of the signs of Allah and their mockery. It has also been said: al-Su'a is a verbal noun in the position of al-isa'ah (evil-doing), so the meaning is: denial was the last of their affair, that is, they died upon it, as if Allah, the Exalted, recompensed them for their evil-doing by sealing their hearts until they died upon denial as a punishment for them. It is also permissible for "al-Su'a" to be the object of "asa'ū," and "an kadhdhabū" to be the predicate of kāna. And whoever puts "ʿāqibata" in the accusative makes it the predicate of "kāna," and "al-Su'a" its subject; it is also permissible for "an kadhdhabū" to be its subject. Al-A'mash read: "asa'ū al-su'u" with "al-su'u" in the nominative.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah originates creation, then repeats it﴾ That is: He creates them first, then He returns them after death alive as they were, ﴿then to Him you will be returned﴾. According to this, the speech shifts from the third person (narrative) to the second person (address). The intended meaning of mentioning the return is recompense for deeds. "Al-khalq" means "those created," and he said "yu'iduhu" (He repeats it) in accordance with the wording "al-khalq."

﴿Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief﴾, that is, the recompense of his disbelief. ﴿And whoever does righteousness, for themselves they prepare [the way]﴾, that is, they make ready [a resting place] for themselves (yumahhidun), meaning yuwatti'un (they lay down a bed or level ground).

Mujahid said: they make the resting places (al-madaji') level in the graves.

Abu 'Ubayda said: "man" (من, whoever) applies to the singular, the dual and the plural, masculine and feminine, and its meaning here is the meaning of the plural. And "yamhadu" (يَمْهَدُ) is in the sense of yaktasibu (earns), ya'malu (works) and yasta'iddu (prepares).

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 30, verses 46–47:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bearers of good tidings﴾, announcing the rain. ﴿And that He may let you taste of His mercy﴾, which is the rain (ghayth) and fertility. ﴿And that the ships may sail﴾ on the sea by those winds ﴿by His command﴾. ﴿And that you may seek﴾ through trade on the sea ﴿of His bounty﴾, which is provision. All of this is by means of the winds.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then they came to them with clear proofs﴾, i.e., with evidences of their truthfulness. ﴿So We took vengeance upon those who committed crime﴾, i.e., We punished those who denied them. ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us﴾, i.e., it was a binding obligation which He imposed upon Himself, ﴿to help the believers﴾, their deliverance along with the messengers from the punishment of the deniers.

All of this is by means of the winds.

**The Verse of God's Statement: ﴿He sends the winds﴾.** Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Raja', al-Nakha'i, Talha ibn Musarrif, and al-A'mash read: "yursilu al-rih" (He sends the wind), without the alif.

**The Verse of God's Statement: ﴿Then they stir up clouds﴾**, that is, they agitate them. **﴿And He spreads them in the sky however He wills﴾**, so if He wills He spreads them for a day, two days, or less or more. **﴿And makes them fragments﴾**, that is, scattered pieces. Most readers pronounce the sin of "kisafan" with a fatha. Abu Razin, Qatada, Ibn 'Amir, Abu Ja'far, and Ibn Abi 'Abla read it with a sukun. Abu 'Ali said: it is possible that it is like sidrah and sidar (a singular and its plural), so the meaning of the two readings is one. **﴿Then you see the rain coming out from within it﴾.** Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Abu al-'Aliya read: "min khalalihi" (from its gaps). We have explained this in (al-Nur: 43). **﴿Then when He strikes with it﴾**, that is, with the rain, **﴿they rejoice﴾**, meaning they are delighted by the rain. **﴿And even though before it was sent down upon them﴾**, the rain, **﴿they were despairing before it﴾**. There are three opinions regarding this repetition.

The first is that it is for emphasis, like His statement: ﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them together﴾ [al-Hijr: 30]. This was said by al-Akhfash and others.

The second is that the first "qabl" (before) refers to the sending down, and the second refers to the rain. This was said by Qutrub. Ibn al-Anbari said: the meaning is "from before the descent of the rain, from before the rain." This is like when one says: "I will come to you before you speak, before you settle in your seat." So the repetition is not rejected, because the two things differ.

The third is that the pronoun in His statement ﴿before it﴾ refers to guidance, even though no mention of it has preceded. So the meaning is: they were despairing before the descent of the rain, before the guidance. When guidance and Islam came, despair left them. Ibn al-Anbari related this from Abu 'Umar al-Duri and Abu Ja'far ibn Qadim. Al-Mublisun (those in despair) are those who have lost hope. The discussion of this has already preceded in (al-An'am: 44).

**﴿So look at the effects of the mercy of God﴾.** Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu 'Amr, and Abu Bakr from 'Asim read: "ila athari" (to the effect). Ibn 'Amir, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from 'Asim read: "ila athari" in the plural. The "mercy" here means the rain, and its "effect" means the vegetation. The meaning is: look at the excellence of its influence upon the earth. **﴿How He gives life to the earth﴾**, that is, how He makes it bring forth plants after there were no plants in it. 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, Abu Raja', Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, and Sulayman al-Taymi read: "kayfa tuhyi" with a raised ta' and a kasra on the ya', and "al-ard" with a fatha on the dad.

**The Verse of God's Statement: ﴿And if We send a wind﴾**, [that is, a wind] that is cold and harmful. When the wind is mentioned in the singular, it is intended to mean punishment. For this reason the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to say when the wind blew: "O Allah, make it winds (of mercy) and do not make it a wind (of punishment)." **﴿Then they see it turned yellow﴾**, meaning the vegetation, and the pronoun refers to the effect. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that they saw the vegetation had turned yellow and dried out. **﴿Then they would surely disbelieve after it﴾**. Its meaning is "they would surely," because the sense of the statement is conditional and consequential. They rejoice at the rain, and they disbelieve when the rain stops from them and the vegetation dries out. Others said: the intended meaning of "God's mercy" is the rain. "Zallu" here means "they became," and "from after it" means that after the yellowing of the vegetation they deny the blessing that had preceded.

What follows is explained in (al-Naml: 80, 81), up to His statement: ﴿God is He who created you from weakness﴾. We have discussed this in (al-Anfal: 66). The commentators said: the meaning is that He created you from water of weakness, which is semen. **﴿Then He made after weakness﴾**, meaning the weakness of childhood, **strength**, the strength of youth. Then He made after the strength of youth the weakness of old age and gray hair. **﴿He creates what He wills﴾**, that is, weakness and strength, youth and gray hair. **﴿And He is the Knowing﴾** of the arrangement of His creation, **﴿the Capable﴾** over what He wills.

**The Verse of God's Statement: ﴿And the Day the Hour is established﴾.** Al-Zajjaj said: "the Hour" in the Qur'an means the hour in which the Resurrection occurs, which is why it is not known which hour that is.

**The Verse of God's Statement: ﴿The criminals will swear﴾**, that is, the polytheists will swear **﴿that they had not remained﴾** in the graves **﴿except an hour. Thus they were deluded﴾**. Ibn Qutayba said: it is said "uffika al-rajul" (the man was deluded) when he is turned away from the truth. So the meaning is that they lied in this situation just as they lied in the world. Others said: God intends to disgrace them on the Day of Resurrection before the believers, so they swear to something whose falsehood will be clear to the believers, and they derive evidence of their lying from the world.

(p-312) Then He mentioned the believers' denial of them in His statement: ﴿But those who were given knowledge and faith will say﴾. Regarding them there are two opinions. The first is that they are the angels. The second is that they are the believers.

**The Verse of God's Statement: ﴿You had remained within the Book of God until the Day of Resurrection﴾.** Regarding this there are two opinions.

The first is that there is a transposition in it, its meaning being: "Those who were given knowledge of the Book of God and faith in God will say." This was said by Ibn Juraij and a group of the commentators.

The second is that it is in its order. Then regarding its meaning there are two opinions. The first is: "You had remained in the knowledge of God." This was said by al-Farra'. The second is: "You had remained in the report of the Book." This was said by Ibn Qutayba.

**The Verse of God's Statement: ﴿So this is the Day of Resurrection﴾**, that is, the day that you used to deny, **﴿but you did not know﴾** in the world that it would occur.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that they saw the vegetation had turned yellow and dried out. **﴿Then they would surely disbelieve after it﴾**. Its meaning is "they would surely," because the sense of the statement is conditional and consequential. They rejoice at the rain, and they disbelieve when the rain stops from them and the vegetation dries out. Others said: the intended meaning of "God's mercy" is the rain. "Zallu" here means "they became," and "from after it" means that after the yellowing of the vegetation they deny the blessing that had preceded.

What follows is explained in (al-Naml: 80, 81), up to His statement: ﴿God is He who created you from weakness﴾. We have discussed this in (al-Anfal: 66). The commentators said: the meaning is that He created you from water of weakness, which is semen. **﴿Then He made after weakness﴾**, meaning the weakness of childhood, **strength**, the strength of youth. Then He made after the strength of youth the weakness of old age and gray hair. **﴿He creates what He wills﴾**, that is, weakness and strength, youth and gray hair. **﴿And He is the Knowing﴾** of the arrangement of His creation, **﴿the Capable﴾** over what He wills.

**The Verse of God's Statement: ﴿And the Day the Hour is established﴾.** Al-Zajjaj said: "the Hour" in the Qur'an means the hour in which the Resurrection occurs, which is why it is not known which hour that is.

**The Verse of God's Statement: ﴿The criminals will swear﴾**, that is, the polytheists will swear **﴿that they had not remained﴾** in the graves **﴿except an hour. Thus they were deluded﴾**. Ibn Qutayba said: it is said "uffika al-rajul" (the man was deluded) when he is turned away from the truth. So the meaning is that they lied in this situation just as they lied in the world. Others said: God intends to disgrace them on the Day of Resurrection before the believers, so they swear to something whose falsehood will be clear to the believers, and they derive evidence of their lying from the world.

(p-312) Then He mentioned the believers' denial of them in His statement: ﴿But those who were given knowledge and faith will say﴾. Regarding them there are two opinions. The first is that they are the angels. The second is that they are the believers.

**The Verse of God's Statement: ﴿You had remained within the Book of God until the Day of Resurrection﴾.** Regarding this there are two opinions.

The first is that there is a transposition in it, its meaning being: "Those who were given knowledge of the Book of God and faith in God will say." This was said by Ibn Juraij and a group of the commentators.

The second is that it is in its order. Then regarding its meaning there are two opinions. The first is: "You had remained in the knowledge of God." This was said by al-Farra'. The second is: "You had remained in the report of the Book." This was said by Ibn Qutayba.

**The Verse of God's Statement: ﴿So this is the Day of Resurrection﴾**, that is, the day that you used to deny, **﴿but you did not know﴾** in the world that it would occur.

**﴿So on that Day, the excuse of those who did wrong will not benefit them﴾.** Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu 'Amr, and Ibn 'Amir read: "la tanfa'u" with a ta'. 'Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read with a ya', because the feminine here is not real (the gender is not true).

Ibn 'Abbas said: no excuse or repentance will be accepted from those who associated partners with God.

**The Verse of God's Statement: ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾**, that is, they will not be asked to seek pleasure (of God) and return in the Hereafter.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 30, verses 58–60:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if you bring them a sign,﴾ that is, like the staff of Musa (Moses) and his hand, ﴿those who disbelieve will surely say, "You are not but falsifiers."﴾ That is, "You, O Muhammad, and your companions, are nothing but people of falsehoods." This is an explanation of their obstinacy. ﴿Thus﴾ that is, just as He sealed their hearts so that they do not affirm the signs, ﴿Allah seals the hearts of those who do not know﴾ the Oneness of Allah. So the cause of the disbelievers' refusal of monotheism is the sealing upon their hearts.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾ concerning your victory and your triumph over your enemy. ﴿And let not those who do not have certainty make you unsteady.﴾ Ya'qub recited it as "yastakhiffannak" with a sukun on the nun, as did Ruh and Zayd in the version "yastakhiffannaka." Al-Zajjaj said: "Let them not provoke you (yastafizzannaka) away from your religion." ﴿Those who do not have certainty﴾ that is, they are misguided doubters. Others said: they do not have certainty regarding the Resurrection and the recompense. Some of the exegetes claimed that this verse is abrogated (mansukha).
